children: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Tuesday granted accelerated approval to neladalkib, a lung cancer therapy now owned by GSK
, following its $10.6B acquisition of Boston-based biopharma Nuvalent earlier this year.

The FDA approved the kinase inhibitor as a late-line option for adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer whose tumors express a specific cancer-causing genetic mutation known as ALK.
The decision came ahead of the Nov. 27 target action date assigned for Nuvalent’s (NUVL) new drug application under the FDA’s priority
The British drugmaker acquired the U.S. company in an all-cash deal worth about $10.6B in July.

The approval is based on the Nuvalent-initiated ALKOVE-1 Phase 1/2 clinical trial, in which patients with ALK-positive NSCLC who had undergone prior tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy indicated an objective response rate of about 31%.
Final FDA approval is subject to
a confirmatory trial. The treatment branded as Nelkarmi is GSK's
second approval in lung cancer this year, after the FDA greenlighted Jideytro, another kinase inhibitor from the London-based firm, in July for adults with NSCLC whose cancers express a gene

title: GSK wins FDA nod for lung cancer therapy added from Nuvalent buyout
